questions.problem: Given that $Q(0,5,2)$ lies on the plane $Π:r\cdot ⟨-6,2,3⟩=16$, find the shortest distance from $P(1,-4,5)$ to $Π.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨0,5,2⟩-⟨1,-4,5⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,9,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨-6,2,3⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-1)\cdot (-6)+9\cdot 2+(-3)\cdot 3|}{\sqrt{(-6)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{3}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|6+18-9|}{\sqrt{36+4+9}} \\  & =\frac{|15|}{\sqrt{49}} \\  & =\frac{15}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-4,-1,5)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $-4x-2y+2z=16.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=-1$ and $y=2$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-4x-2y+2z & =16 \\ -4(-1)-2(2)+2z & =16 \\ 2z & =16 \\ z & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(-1,2,8)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨-1,2,8⟩-⟨-4,-1,5⟩ \\  & =⟨3,3,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩.$ So, for the plane $Π,$ we have $n=⟨-4,-2,2⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|3\cdot (-4)+3\cdot (-2)+3\cdot 2|}{\sqrt{(-4)^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-12-6+6|}{\sqrt{16+4+4}} \\  & =\frac{|\,-12\,|}{\sqrt{24}} \\  & =\sqrt{6}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-1,3,-4)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $6x+2y+3z=9.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's start by picking a point on the plane. To do that, we simply substitute some concrete values for $x$ and $y$ into the equation and solve for $z.$ Let's choose $x=1$ and $y=0$ (though it doesn't really matter what values we choose). Solving for $z,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}6x+2y+3z & =9 \\ 6(1)+2(0)+3z & =9 \\ 3z & =3 \\ z & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the point $Q(1,0,1)$ which lies on the plane.

Computing $\overset{\to }{PQ},$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨1,0,1⟩-⟨-1,3,-4⟩ \\  & =⟨2,-3,5⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We also need a normal vector to the plane. For any Cartesian equation of a plane $ax+by+cz=d,$ the normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩.$ So, for the plane $Π,$ we have $n=⟨6,2,3⟩.$ 

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|2\cdot 6+(-3)\cdot 2+5\cdot 3|}{\sqrt{{6}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{3}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|12-6+15|}{\sqrt{36+4+9}} \\  & =\frac{|21|}{\sqrt{49}} \\  & =\frac{21}{7} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
